name: Misure
description: I nomi delle misure e delle caratteristiche dei segnali.

terms.definition: The time a signal takes to go from low to high, usually from 10 to 90 percent.
terms.example: The rise time is twelve nanoseconds.

terms.definition: The time a signal takes to go from high to low.
terms.example: The fall time is longer than the rise time.

terms.definition: Small random changes in the timing of a signal's edges.
terms.example: The clock jitter is below fifty picoseconds.

terms.definition: The small AC variation on top of a DC voltage.
terms.example: The ripple on the 1.8 volt rail is twenty millivolts.

terms.definition: A small unwanted current that flows when a device should be off.
terms.example: The leakage current increases a lot at high temperature.

terms.definition: How much power a device uses.
terms.example: We reduced the power consumption in stop mode.

terms.definition: A picture of many bits on top of each other, used to check signal quality.
terms.example: The eye diagram is wide open at 480 megabits per second.

terms.definition: The level of noise when there is no signal.
terms.example: The noise floor of the ADC is about two LSB.

terms.definition: When a signal goes above its final value after an edge.
terms.example: The overshoot is ten percent of the amplitude.

terms.definition: When a signal goes below its final value after an edge.
terms.example: We saw undershoot below ground on the reset line.

terms.definition: The time a signal needs to become stable after a change.
terms.example: The DAC settling time is five microseconds.

terms.definition: The time between a change at the input and the change at the output.
terms.example: The propagation delay of the buffer is three nanoseconds.

terms.definition: The percentage of time a signal is high in each period.
terms.example: The PWM runs at fifty percent duty cycle.

terms.definition: The range of frequencies a system can handle.
terms.example: We need an oscilloscope with at least one gigahertz of bandwidth.

terms.definition: How many samples per second an ADC or an instrument takes.
terms.example: The sampling rate is one megasample per second.

terms.definition: The smallest change a system can detect or produce.
terms.example: It is a twelve-bit ADC, so the resolution is about one millivolt.

terms.definition: How close a measurement is to the true value.
terms.example: The accuracy of the reference is plus or minus 0.1 percent.

terms.definition: A constant error added to every measurement.
terms.example: We calibrated the offset at room temperature.

terms.definition: How much a circuit amplifies a signal.
terms.example: The gain error is below 0.5 percent.

terms.definition: How well the output follows a straight line compared to the input.
terms.example: We measured the ADC linearity with a slow ramp.

terms.definition: How much stronger the signal is than the noise, in decibels.
terms.example: The signal-to-noise ratio is seventy decibels.

terms.definition: The current a device uses when it is on but not doing any work.
terms.example: The quiescent current of the LDO is only one microamp.

terms.definition: The difference between the highest and the lowest value of a signal.
terms.example: The noise is five millivolts peak-to-peak.

terms.definition: A kind of average that tells the effective value of an AC signal.
terms.example: The RMS noise is one millivolt.

terms.definition: How long data must be stable before the clock edge.
terms.example: We have a setup time violation at high temperature.

terms.definition: How long data must stay stable after the clock edge.
terms.example: The hold time margin is only 200 picoseconds.

terms.definition: How fast a signal can change, in volts per microsecond.
terms.example: The op-amp slew rate limits the output at high frequency.

terms.definition: When a signal on one wire disturbs a nearby wire.
terms.example: We saw crosstalk between the clock and the data line.

terms.definition: A short voltage change on ground when many outputs switch together.
terms.example: Ground bounce caused false triggers on the input.

terms.definition: A slow change of a value over time or temperature.
terms.example: The oscillator drift is ten ppm over temperature.

terms.definition: How much a value can differ from its nominal value.
terms.example: These resistors have a one percent tolerance.

terms.definition: How much data a system can transfer in a given time.
terms.example: The DMA throughput is twenty megabytes per second.

terms.definition: The delay between a request and the response.
terms.example: The interrupt latency is twelve clock cycles.
